name: Runna
tagline: Subscription running app that builds adaptive race training plans and pushes the workouts to your watch.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The plan generator itself is not mysterious: periodization is arithmetic, pace zones come from a recent race time and a formula, and a coding agent can produce a sane 12 week marathon build in an afternoon. What you cannot one-shot is the part you actually touch every day, which is the structured workout landing on your Garmin or Apple Watch with intervals and target paces already programmed. Garmin's training API is partner-gated, and pushing workouts to an Apple Watch means a real native app, not a web page. So you get a credible plan and a calendar, and then you read your intervals off your phone like it is 2014. Fine for self-coached runners, annoying for everyone else.
coreLoopDIY: Generates a periodized running plan from your goal race, date, current weekly mileage and a recent time, then exports it to your calendar and tracks completed sessions.
requirements: A recent race time or time trial to seed pace zones
A calendar app that accepts ICS subscriptions
Willingness to read workouts off your phone instead of your wrist
whatYouLose: Structured workouts pushed to Garmin, Coros or Apple Watch with intervals and target paces pre-loaded
Plans designed and sanity-checked by actual coaches rather than your agent's interpretation of periodization
Automatic adaptation when you miss a week, get sick, or run every easy run too hard
Guided strength, mobility and physio sessions with video
A polished mobile app with notifications, streaks and a community that mildly shames you into going outside
moatNotes: The watch integrations are the product. Everything else is a spreadsheet with a nice font.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value is not knowing what Tuesday's session is, it is not having to think about it and not having to transcribe 6 x 800m at 4:12 into a watch at the track. Runna sits in the gap between a free generic PDF plan and a human coach at ten times the price, and the gap is mostly logistics: sync, adaptation, reminders, and the feeling that a coach somewhere signed off on the volume curve. A DIY plan generator covers the thinking and none of the logistics, which is exactly backwards from where the friction is.
notes: Build this if you are already self-coached and just want the arithmetic done; buy it if the watch sync is the whole reason you were tempted.
prompt:
Build a local-first running training plan generator called "Plan".

Stack: Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, running entirely on localhost. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics. Single user.

Core features:
1. Setup form: goal race distance (5k, 10k, half, marathon), goal race date, current average weekly mileage, days per week available, and one recent race result (distance + time) or a recent time trial.
2. From the recent result, compute VDOT-style equivalent paces using the Riegel formula (t2 = t1 * (d2/d1)^1.06) and derive five pace zones: easy, marathon, threshold, interval, repetition. Show the formula and the numbers so the user can sanity check them.
3. Generate a periodized plan from today to race day: base, build, peak, taper. Cap weekly mileage growth at 10 percent, insert a down week every fourth week, and taper over the final 2 to 3 weeks depending on race distance. Each week gets one long run, one quality session (alternate threshold and interval), and the rest easy.
4. Render the plan as a week-by-week view and a single session detail view with warmup, main set written as reps x distance at target pace range, and cooldown.
5. Logging: mark a session done, skipped, or modified, with actual distance, time and a 1 to 5 effort rating. Store in SQLite.
6. Simple adaptation: if a user misses more than 30 percent of a week, regenerate the remaining plan from the current actual mileage instead of the original ramp. Show a banner explaining what changed and why.
7. Export: serve an ICS feed at /api/calendar.ics containing every future session with the full workout in the description, so it can be subscribed to from any calendar app.
8. GPX import: accept a dropped .gpx file, parse distance and elapsed time, and offer to attach it to the nearest planned session.

Explicitly out of scope: watch sync of any kind, Garmin or Strava OAuth, push notifications, strength or mobility video, social feeds, coaching chat, payments.

Keep all tunable constants (ramp cap, down week cadence, taper length, zone percentages) in a single config.ts with comments, so the training philosophy can be edited in one place. Put nothing in .env since there are no secrets. Ship a README with how to run it and a blunt paragraph stating that this is not coached advice and that the ramp caps are conservative defaults, not medicine.
